review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

12:1.sourceText: Περὶ δὲ τῶν πνευματικῶν, ἀδελφοί, οὐ θέλω ὑμᾶς ἀγνοεῖν.
12:1.targetText: Now about spiritual gifts, brothers, I do not want you to be uninformed.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

12:2.sourceText: Οἴδατε ὅτι ὅτε ἔθνη ἦτε πρὸς τὰ εἴδωλα τὰ ἄφωνα ὡς ἂν ἤγεσθε ἀπαγόμενοι.
12:2.targetText: You know that when you were pagans, you were influenced and led astray to mute idols.

groups.note: ἤγεσθε ("you were led") is rendered you were influenced.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB has no separate word for ὡς ἄν ("however, as") here.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle ἀπαγόμενοι ("being led away") to the main verb; the Greek has no καί here.

12:3.sourceText: διὸ γνωρίζω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐδεὶς ἐν Πνεύματι Θεοῦ λαλῶν λέγει ΑΝΑΘΕΜΑ ΙΗΣΟΥΣ, καὶ οὐδεὶς δύναται εἰπεῖν ΚΥΡΙΟΣ ΙΗΣΟΥΣ, εἰ μὴ ἐν Πνεύματι Ἁγίῳ.
12:3.targetText: Therefore I inform you that no one who is speaking by the Spirit of God says, “Jesus be cursed,” and no one can say, “Jesus is Lord,” except by the Holy Spirit.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a verb for the curse; the Greek has none.
English supplies the copula; the Greek has no verb.

12:4.sourceText: Διαιρέσεις δὲ χαρισμάτων εἰσίν, τὸ δὲ αὐτὸ Πνεῦμα·
12:4.targetText: There are different gifts, but the same Spirit.

groups.note: Διαιρέσεις ("varieties, distributions") is rendered different.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening δέ untranslated.

12:5.sourceText: καὶ διαιρέσεις διακονιῶν εἰσιν, καὶ ὁ αὐτὸς Κύριος·
12:5.targetText: There are different ministries, but the same Lord.

groups.note: καί ("and") is rendered but.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening καί untranslated.

12:6.sourceText: καὶ διαιρέσεις ἐνεργημάτων εἰσίν, ὁ δὲ αὐτὸς Θεός ὁ ἐνεργῶν τὰ πάντα ἐν πᾶσιν.
12:6.targetText: There are different ways of working, but the same God works all things in all people.

groups.note: The article and participle ὁ ἐνεργῶν ("the one working") are rendered works.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening καί untranslated.

12:7.sourceText: ἑκάστῳ δὲ δίδοται ἡ φανέρωσις τοῦ Πνεύματος πρὸς τὸ συμφέρον.
12:7.targetText: Now to each one the manifestation of the Spirit is given for the common good.

12:8.sourceText: ᾧ μὲν γὰρ διὰ τοῦ Πνεύματος δίδοται λόγος σοφίας, ἄλλῳ δὲ λόγος γνώσεως κατὰ τὸ αὐτὸ Πνεῦμα,
12:8.targetText: To one there is given through the Spirit the message of wisdom, to another the message of knowledge by the same Spirit,

unmappedSource.reason: The correlative μέν has no English counterpart.
BSB leaves the connective γάρ untranslated.
BSB leaves this δέ untranslated and lists the next gift with a comma.

12:9.sourceText: ἑτέρῳ πίστις ἐν τῷ αὐτῷ Πνεύματι, ἄλλῳ δὲ χαρίσματα ἰαμάτων ἐν τῷ ἑνὶ Πνεύματι,
12:9.targetText: to another faith by the same Spirit, to another gifts of healing by that one Spirit,

groups.note: The article τῷ ("the") is rendered that.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves this δέ untranslated and lists the next gift with a comma.

12:10.sourceText: ἄλλῳ δὲ ἐνεργήματα δυνάμεων, ἄλλῳ δὲ προφητεία, ἄλλῳ δὲ διακρίσεις πνευμάτων, ἑτέρῳ γένη γλωσσῶν, ἄλλῳ δὲ ἑρμηνεία γλωσσῶν·
12:10.targetText: to another the working of miracles, to another prophecy, to another distinguishing between spirits, to another speaking in various tongues, and to still another the interpretation of tongues.

groups.note: γένη ("kinds") is rendered various.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves these δέ untranslated and lists the next gift with a comma.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies speaking in; the Greek says "kinds of tongues".
English adds still; the Greek has only ἄλλῳ ("to another").

12:11.sourceText: πάντα δὲ ταῦτα ἐνεργεῖ τὸ ἓν καὶ τὸ αὐτὸ Πνεῦμα, διαιροῦν ἰδίᾳ ἑκάστῳ καθὼς βούλεται.
12:11.targetText: All these are the work of one and the same Spirit, who apportions them to each one as He determines.

groups.note: ἐνεργεῖ ("works, produces") is rendered are the work of.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB does not render ἰδίᾳ ("individually") separately.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object; the Greek has no pronoun.

12:12.sourceText: Καθάπερ γὰρ τὸ σῶμα ἕν ἐστιν καὶ μέλη πολλὰ ἔχει, πάντα δὲ τὰ μέλη τοῦ σώματος πολλὰ ὄντα ἕν ἐστιν σῶμα, οὕτως καὶ ὁ Χριστός·
12:12.targetText: The body is a unit, though it is composed of many parts. And although its parts are many, they all form one body. So it is with Christ.

groups.note: καί ("and") is rendered though.
ἔχει ("has") is rendered is composed of.
τοῦ σώματος ("of the body") is rendered its.
The participle ὄντα ("being") is rendered although … are.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves Καθάπερ ("just as") untranslated; the comparison is carried by So.
BSB leaves the connective γάρ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves καί ("also") untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a frame for the comparison; the Greek has no verb here.

12:13.sourceText: καὶ γὰρ ἐν ἑνὶ Πνεύματι ἡμεῖς πάντες εἰς ἓν σῶμα ἐβαπτίσθημεν, εἴτε Ἰουδαῖοι εἴτε Ἕλληνες, εἴτε δοῦλοι εἴτε ἐλεύθεροι. καὶ πάντες ἓν Πνεῦμα ἐποτίσθημεν.
12:13.targetText: For in one Spirit we were all baptized into one body, whether Jews or Greeks, slave or free, and we were all given one Spirit to drink.

groups.note: καὶ γάρ ("for indeed") is rendered For.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB has no word for this εἴτε; it gives slave or free without a second whether.

12:14.sourceText: καὶ γὰρ τὸ σῶμα οὐκ ἔστιν ἓν μέλος ἀλλὰ πολλά.
12:14.targetText: For the body does not consist of one part, but of many.

groups.note: καὶ γάρ ("for indeed") is rendered For.
ἔστιν ("is") is rendered does … consist of, and BSB repeats of before many.

12:15.sourceText: ἐὰν εἴπῃ ὁ πούς Ὅτι οὐκ εἰμὶ χείρ, οὐκ εἰμὶ ἐκ τοῦ σώματος, οὐ παρὰ τοῦτο οὐκ ἔστιν ἐκ τοῦ σώματος.
12:15.targetText: If the foot should say, “Because I am not a hand, I do not belong to the body,” that would not make it any less a part of the body.

groups.note: παρὰ τοῦτο ("for this reason") is rendered as the subject that.
The second negative (literally "it is not … not of the body") is rendered any less.
ἔστιν ("it is") is recast as would … make it.

12:16.sourceText: καὶ ἐὰν εἴπῃ τὸ οὖς Ὅτι οὐκ εἰμὶ ὀφθαλμός, οὐκ εἰμὶ ἐκ τοῦ σώματος, οὐ παρὰ τοῦτο οὐκ ἔστιν ἐκ τοῦ σώματος.
12:16.targetText: And if the ear should say, “Because I am not an eye, I do not belong to the body,” that would not make it any less a part of the body.

groups.note: παρὰ τοῦτο ("for this reason") is rendered as the subject that.
The second negative (literally "it is not … not of the body") is rendered any less.
ἔστιν ("it is") is recast as would … make it.

12:17.sourceText: εἰ ὅλον τὸ σῶμα ὀφθαλμός, ποῦ ἡ ἀκοή; εἰ ὅλον ἀκοή, ποῦ ἡ ὄσφρησις;
12:17.targetText: If the whole body were an eye, where would the sense of hearing be? If the whole body were an ear, where would the sense of smell be?

groups.note: σῶμα is understood again in the second question, where BSB repeats the body.
ἀκοή ("hearing") is rendered ear here.

12:18.sourceText: νῦν δὲ ὁ Θεὸς ἔθετο τὰ μέλη, ἓν ἕκαστον αὐτῶν ἐν τῷ σώματι καθὼς ἠθέλησεν.
12:18.targetText: But in fact, God has arranged the members of the body, every one of them, according to His design.

groups.note: BSB's Greek text has a different form of this word here, with the same meaning.
ἐν ("in") the body is rendered of the body.
ἠθέλησεν ("He willed") is rendered His design.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

12:19.sourceText: εἰ δὲ ἦν τὰ πάντα ἓν μέλος, ποῦ τὸ σῶμα;
12:19.targetText: If they were all one part, where would the body be?

12:20.sourceText: νῦν δὲ πολλὰ μὲν μέλη, ἓν δὲ σῶμα.
12:20.targetText: As it is, there are many parts, but one body.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves this δέ untranslated.
The correlative μέν has no English counterpart.

12:21.sourceText: οὐ δύναται δὲ ὁ ὀφθαλμὸς εἰπεῖν τῇ χειρί Χρείαν σου οὐκ ἔχω, ἢ πάλιν ἡ κεφαλὴ τοῖς ποσίν Χρείαν ὑμῶν οὐκ ἔχω·
12:21.targetText: The eye cannot say to the hand, “I do not need you.” Nor can the head say to the feet, “I do not need you.”

groups.note: οὐ δύναται ("is not able") is rendered cannot; BSB repeats the verb as can after Nor.
εἰπεῖν is understood again with the head, where BSB repeats say.
Χρείαν … ἔχω ("I have need") is rendered I do … need.
ἤ ("or") is rendered Nor, carrying the negative into the second clause.
Χρείαν … ἔχω ("I have need") is rendered I do … need.

12:22.sourceText: ἀλλὰ πολλῷ μᾶλλον τὰ δοκοῦντα μέλη τοῦ σώματος ἀσθενέστερα ὑπάρχειν ἀναγκαῖά ἐστιν,
12:22.targetText: On the contrary, the parts of the body that seem to be weaker are indispensable,

unmappedSource.reason: BSB does not render πολλῷ μᾶλλον ("much more") separately.

12:23.sourceText: καὶ ἃ δοκοῦμεν ἀτιμότερα εἶναι τοῦ σώματος, τούτοις τιμὴν περισσοτέραν περιτίθεμεν, καὶ τὰ ἀσχήμονα ἡμῶν εὐσχημοσύνην περισσοτέραν ἔχει,
12:23.targetText: and the parts we consider less honorable, we treat with greater honor. And our unpresentable parts are treated with special modesty,

groups.note: The relative ἅ ("which") is rendered the parts.
περιτίθεμεν ("we put on, bestow") is rendered we treat with.
ἔχει ("has") is rendered are treated with.

12:24.sourceText: τὰ δὲ εὐσχήμονα ἡμῶν οὐ χρείαν ἔχει. ἀλλὰ ὁ θεὸς συνεκέρασεν τὸ σῶμα, τῷ ὑστερουμένῳ περισσοτέραν δοὺς τιμήν,
12:24.targetText: whereas our presentable parts have no such need.  But God has composed the body and has given greater honor to the parts that lacked it,

groups.note: Article and participle τῷ ὑστερουμένῳ ("the one lacking") form one unit.

12:25.sourceText: ἵνα μὴ ᾖ σχίσμα ἐν τῷ σώματι, ἀλλὰ τὸ αὐτὸ ὑπὲρ ἀλλήλων μεριμνῶσιν τὰ μέλη.
12:25.targetText: so that there should be no division in the body, but that its members should have mutual concern for one another.

groups.note: ἵνα governs both clauses; BSB repeats that before the second.
τὸ αὐτό ("the same") is rendered mutual.
μεριμνῶσιν ("they may care") is rendered should have … concern.

ἐκ μέρους ("individually") is rendered each of you.
